blockingFindings.title: Activity artifact references omit logical-key resolution
blockingFindings.issue: resolveActivityReference only matched hash and relativePath, so a stored Activity artifact reference identified by a validated catalog logicalKey was treated as unresolved and omitted.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Match descriptor.logicalKey against reference.id in resolveActivityReference while retaining optional omission for zero matches.
blockingFindings.rationale: R7 explicitly permits relativePath, logicalKey, and validated kind-pair lookup for stored Activity references. Repaired in this review.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact relation arrays did not enforce their contract limit
blockingFindings.issue: ArtifactDescriptorView accepted duplicate relation IDs and up to MAX_PUBLIC_COLLECTION_ITEMS rather than enforcing unique activityIds, nodeIds, and taskIds with MAX_IDS_PER_ARTIFACT.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add configurable collection bounds and uniqueness validation to requirePublicStringList, and apply MAX_IDS_PER_ARTIFACT plus unique=true to ArtifactDescriptorView relation arrays.
blockingFindings.rationale: R7 mandates unique relation arrays bounded by MAX_IDS_PER_ARTIFACT. Repaired in this review.

blockingFindings.title: Version discovery rejected valid versions above 999
blockingFindings.issue: CanonicalVersionDirectoryEntry and directory enumeration required exactly three digits, although FlowVersion.pathSegment supports positive safe-integer versions such as 1000 and the available-version contract is not limited to three-digit values.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Accept numeric normalized directory names according to FlowVersion.pathSegment and classify malformed or unsafe numeric identities as CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT.
blockingFindings.rationale: R8 requires positive safe-integer available Flow Versions and bounded discovery; rejecting valid normalized versions above 999 violates that contract. Repaired in this review.

blockingFindings.summary: Activity artifact references omit logical-key resolution
Artifact relation arrays did not enforce their contract limit
Version discovery rejected valid versions above 999

blockingFindings.title: Activity sequence accepted zero
blockingFindings.issue: ActivityItem validation accepted sequence: 0 even though R11 requires a positive integer when sequence is non-null.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Reject non-null sequence values below 1 in ActivityItem; repaired in this review.
blockingFindings.rationale: R11 explicitly requires positive Activity sequence values. The constructor now enforces that invariant.

blockingFindings.title: Activity timestamps lacked ISO validation
blockingFindings.issue: ActivityItem validation previously checked Timing and Outcome timestamps only as bounded strings, allowing non-ISO values.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Route Timing.startedAt, Timing.finishedAt, and Outcome.confirmedAt through strict ISO datetime validation; repaired in this review.
blockingFindings.rationale: R11 requires ISO8601 timestamp fields. The public validators now enforce the datetime format.

blockingFindings.title: Hash references bypassed catalog kind pairing
blockingFindings.issue: ReferenceResolver.resolve treated kind: hash as a standalone hash lookup, allowing a reference to resolve without the required validated catalog kind pairing.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Remove the standalone hash branch and resolve non-path/non-logical kinds only through the descriptor kind plus validated path/hash pair; repaired in this review.
blockingFindings.rationale: R7 requires exact catalog lookup: path and logical references use their dedicated fields, while other kinds must be bound to the validated descriptor kind.

blockingFindings.summary: Hash references bypassed catalog kind pairing

blockingFindings.title: Confirmed NodeResult artifact references were validated only when paged
blockingFindings.issue: A confirmed Activity's required NodeResult artifact reference could be hidden by page, cursor, or datetime filtering and avoid catalog resolution.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Validate all confirmed Activity result references during canonical catalog reading; repaired via ReferenceResolver.validateCanonicalActivityResults().
blockingFindings.rationale: R7 requires unresolved canonical artifact relations to produce CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT regardless of projection pagination.

blockingFindings.title: Version discovery did not bound ignored directory entries
blockingFindings.issue: Non-numeric entries were enumerated without contributing to the MAX_AVAILABLE_FLOW_VERSIONS limit.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Count every directory entry before filtering numeric Version names; repaired in readVersionDirectoryEntries().
blockingFindings.rationale: R8 requires bounded directory enumeration and failure at the limit-plus-one entry.

blockingFindings.summary: Confirmed NodeResult artifact references were validated only when paged
Version discovery did not bound ignored directory entries

blockingFindings.title: Canonical bounded-file violations use the wrong public error code
blockingFindings.issue: readBoundedFile() previously mapped canonical file identity failures and MAX_* size violations to CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT for canonical identity and size-limit violations, while preserving caller-specific request-file codes and unreadable codes for actual I/O failures.
blockingFindings.rationale: R8 requires canonical identity and bounded-record violations to be distinguished from missing, permission, and read failures. Repaired in readBoundedFile().

blockingFindings.summary: Canonical bounded-file violations use the wrong public error code

blockingFindings.title: Reference resolution policy is duplicated across resolver methods
blockingFindings.issue: resolve() and resolveActivityReference() independently contained the same catalog-match, optional-omission, and inconsistency-error logic.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Route both methods through the shared private #resolve() helper so lookup and error semantics remain identical.
blockingFindings.rationale: The project coding rules require repeated implementation patterns in two or more locations to be extracted into a common helper. Repaired in src/flow/query.js.

blockingFindings.summary: Reference resolution policy is duplicated across resolver methods

blockingFindings.title: ReferenceResolver rejects valid digest-bound canonical references
blockingFindings.issue: Non-path/non-logical references were matched only by descriptor.kind plus relativePath, but canonical Activity results can bind a validated kind or logical key to the descriptor content hash. Such valid references caused the entire Activity projection to fail instead of returning the deterministic public artifactId.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Match a SHA-256 reference id against descriptor.hash while requiring the validated descriptor kind or logicalKey; retain exact path and logical-key matching and ambiguity errors.
blockingFindings.rationale: R7 requires valid stored Artifact references to resolve through the validated catalog and be replaced with deterministic public artifactIds. Repaired in src/flow/query.js.

blockingFindings.summary: ReferenceResolver rejects valid digest-bound canonical references

blockingFindings.title: Catalog artifact I/O failures are misclassified as integrity errors
blockingFindings.issue: catalog.verify() errors were all projected as CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT, including missing, permission, and other canonical Artifact read failures.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Classify filesystem read errors and missing canonical Artifact paths as CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE while preserving schema, digest, identity, and catalog-integrity failures as CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT. Repaired in the catalog verification catch branch.
blockingFindings.rationale: R8 mandates CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE for read, permission, and missing-file failures. The implementation now distinguishes these errors before emitting the catalog integrity error.

blockingFindings.summary: Catalog artifact I/O failures are misclassified as integrity errors
